commitResults.messageTitle: Added commands feature with corrct output
added subclasses for new task types
added task conter changes structured statments
added logic in sub classes for error
Add SE-EDU coding and Git conventions to AGENTS.md
commitResults.messageBody:
Document the SE-EDU Java coding standard and Git conventions as
project-specific requirements, and normalize list markers to
hyphens for consistency. This ensures all future edits and
commits in the repository follow a single, explicit standard
rather than relying on implicit conventions.

Group Jeff, Task, Todo, Deadline, and Event under a single
lowercase jeff package, per the SE-EDU Java coding standard
(every class belongs in a meaningful package). This also makes
it possible to add a Storage class in the same package that can
reference Task and its subclasses, needed for the upcoming
save/load feature.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add toSaveFormat to Task and its subclasses
commitResults.messageBody:
Add a toSaveFormat() method, mirroring the existing toString()
pattern, so each task can encode itself as a single pipe-delimited
line (type | done-flag | description | extra fields). This is the
on-disk representation the upcoming Storage class will read and
write.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add Storage class for reading and writing task data
commitResults.messageBody:
Introduce Storage, which loads a List<Task> from a save file and
writes one back, using the pipe-delimited toSaveFormat() encoding.
Missing save files and corrupted lines are handled gracefully
(empty list / skipped line) rather than crashing the chatbot.
Not yet wired into Jeff.

commitResults.messageTitle: Load and save tasks automatically in Jeff
commitResults.messageBody:
Load history from ./data/jeff.txt on startup, and save it back
via Storage after every mutation (add, mark, unmark, delete), so
the task list survives across runs without any explicit save
command. Ignore the generated data/ folder since it holds runtime
state, not source.

Bring in automatic save/load of tasks to and from
./data/jeff.txt: package reorganization under jeff, the
toSaveFormat() encoding on Task and its subclasses, the Storage
class, and its wiring into Jeff so the task list persists across
runs without any explicit save command.

commitResults.messageTitle: Store Deadline's by date as a LocalDate
commitResults.messageBody:
Parse the /by argument with LocalDate.parse (yyyy-mm-dd), instead
of keeping it as a plain String, so date comparisons and range
queries are possible later. Print it back as "MMM dd yyyy" (e.g.
Oct 15 2019), and reject blank or wrongly formatted input with a
clear error message rather than accepting anything.

commitResults.messageTitle: Store Event's from/to dates as LocalDate
commitResults.messageBody:
Same treatment as Deadline: parse /from and /to with LocalDate.parse
(yyyy-mm-dd) instead of storing them as plain Strings, print them
back as "MMM dd yyyy", and reject blank or wrongly formatted input
with a message naming which argument failed.

Bring in date/time understanding for deadlines and events: parse
/by, /from, and /to arguments as java.time.LocalDate (yyyy-mm-dd
input), print them as "MMM dd yyyy", and store them in ISO format
on disk so saved dates round-trip correctly.

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract TaskList to own the task collection
commitResults.messageBody:
Move the task-storing List<Task> and its add/remove/get/size
operations out of Jeff and into a new TaskList class. Jeff now
delegates to a TaskList instance instead of manipulating a static
list field directly; behavior is unchanged.

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract Ui to own user interaction
commitResults.messageBody:
Move all printing (banner, divider, task confirmations, errors)
and the input Scanner out of Jeff and into a new Ui class. Jeff
now delegates to a Ui instance instead of calling System.out and
Scanner directly; behavior and message wording are unchanged.

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract Parser to make sense of user input
commitResults.messageBody:
Move the Command enum, command-word/argument splitting, the
deadline/event "/label" splitting, and task-number parsing out of
Jeff and into a new Parser class. Jeff now delegates to Parser
instead of parsing raw input itself; behavior is unchanged.

Jeff is now a thin orchestrator over Ui, Storage, Parser, and
TaskList, completing the minimal OOP extraction.

Move Ui to a new jeff.ui sub-package, replacing the flat jeff
package, as part of organizing the codebase into suitable Java
packages. Update Ui's own reference to Task, and Jeff (which
creates and uses a Ui instance), with the new explicit imports.

Move Storage to a new jeff.storage sub-package, replacing the
flat jeff package, as part of organizing the codebase into
suitable Java packages. Update Storage's own references to Task,
Todo, Deadline, and Event, and Jeff (which creates and uses a
Storage instance), with the new explicit imports.

commitResults.messageTitle: Move task classes into jeff.task package
commitResults.messageBody:
Group Task, Todo, Deadline, Event, and TaskList under a new
jeff.task sub-package, replacing the flat jeff package, as part

import.
Move Task, Todo, Deadline, Event, and TaskList into jeff.task.

Move Ui into jeff.ui.

commitResults.messageTitle: Fix cross-package Javadoc links after package split
commitResults.messageBody:
Task and TaskList had {@link Storage}/{@link Ui} references left
over from when everything lived in one flat jeff package. Now
that Storage and Ui live in jeff.storage and jeff.ui, qualify
those links with their full package name so they still resolve.

Bring the OOP extraction and package reorganization work onto
master as a single branch, rather than the separate
branch-A-MoreOOP/branch-A-Packages(-*) branches they were
originally done on:

- Extract Ui, Storage, Parser, and TaskList out of Jeff, so it
  becomes a thin orchestrator (the A-MoreOOP increment).
- Organize all classes into suitable sub-packages (jeff.task,
  jeff.ui, jeff.storage, jeff.parser) instead of one flat jeff
  package (the A-Packages increment).

Bring in Gradle build support (build.gradle, gradle wrapper)
from the course's add-gradle-support branch, so the project can
be built and run via Gradle instead of raw javac/java commands.

commitResults.messageTitle: Point Gradle build at jeff.Jeff instead of the template class
commitResults.messageBody:
The merged add-gradle-support branch's build.gradle still named
the course template's seedu.duke.Duke as the application main
class and duke.jar as the shadow jar output. Update both to
match this project's actual entry point (jeff.Jeff) and name
(jeff.jar), so `gradlew run`/`gradlew shadowJar` work correctly.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add JUnit tests for Task and Todo
commitResults.messageBody:
Cover Task's description validation, done/not-done status
transitions, and toString/toSaveFormat output, plus Todo's
overrides of the same. First step of adding JUnit test coverage
across the codebase (A-JUnit).

commitResults.messageTitle: Add JUnit tests for Deadline and Event
commitResults.messageBody:
Cover the date-parsing logic in both classes: blank fields,
malformed dates, whitespace trimming, and the MMM dd yyyy /
ISO-8601 formatting in toString and toSaveFormat. This is the
most bug-prone part of these classes, so it gets the most cases.

Cover the empty/pre-populated constructors (including that the
pre-populated one copies its input rather than aliasing it),
add, remove, and getTasks.

Cover parseCommandType (every recognized word, unknown/empty
input, case sensitivity), getArguments, splitDeadlineArgs and
splitEventArgs (valid input and missing segments), and
parseTaskIndex (valid, non-numeric, and out-of-range input).

Cover loading from a missing file (empty list, no crash), a full
save/load round trip via a temp file, auto-creating a missing
parent directory on save, and skipping corrupted lines (unknown
type letter, too few fields) on load without losing the rest.

Cover message indentation, the divider, welcome/bye/error text,
task-list/added/removed/marked/unmarked formatting (via
System.out redirection), and readCommand for both an available
line and end-of-input (via System.in redirection).

This completes JUnit coverage of every non-trivial public method
across Task, Todo, Deadline, Event, TaskList, Parser, Storage,
and Ui. Jeff's main() itself is left untested, since it's a thin
stdin/stdout-driven loop rather than a unit of logic.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add missing Javadoc to Task, Todo, Deadline, and Event
commitResults.messageBody:
Add a class-level header to Task, and method-level Javadoc to
every constructor and public method across all four classes
(including the toString/toSaveFormat overrides), so each
documents its parameters, return value, and thrown exceptions
where applicable. Deadline, Event, TaskList, Parser, Storage, and
Ui already had most of their public API documented from earlier
increments; this fills the remaining gaps.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add missing Javadoc to Storage and Jeff
commitResults.messageBody:
Document Storage's constructor, plus Jeff's class header and
main() method (its only previously-undocumented public member).
Combined with the earlier Task/Todo/Deadline/Event commit, every
non-private class and method in the codebase now has a Javadoc
header, and non-trivial private methods already did from earlier
increments.

commitResults.messageTitle: Wrap Ui.showTaskRemoved to fit the 120-char line limit
commitResults.messageBody:
showTaskRemoved's message-building line was 121 characters, one
over the SE-EDU coding standard's line-length limit. Wrap it the
same way showTaskList already wraps its own multi-part message.

Add a description accessor to Task, and a find(keyword) method
to TaskList that returns the tasks whose description contains
the given keyword, in list order. This is the data-layer piece
of the Level-9 "find" feature; command wiring follows separately.

Add "find" to the recognized Command words. No new argument-
splitting helper is needed: getArguments already extracts the
keyword the same way it extracts a todo's description.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add Ui.showMatchingTasks for the find command
commitResults.messageBody:
Extract the numbered-list printing shared by showTaskList and the
new showMatchingTasks into a private showNumberedTasks helper, so
"find" results print the same way "list" results do, just under
a different header.

commitResults.messageTitle: Wire the find command into Jeff
commitResults.messageBody:
Add the FIND case: rejects a blank keyword with an error, same as
other commands with required arguments, otherwise looks up
matching tasks via TaskList.find and shows them via
Ui.showMatchingTasks. Completes the Level-9 "find" feature.

Add missing Javadoc across Task, Todo, Deadline, Event, Storage,
and Jeff, completing header-comment coverage of every non-private
class/method and non-trivial private method (A-JavaDoc).

Fix the one SE-EDU coding-standard violation found on audit: a
121-character line in Ui.showTaskRemoved, wrapped to fit the
120-char limit (A-CodingStandard).

Add the "find KEYWORD" command: Task.getDescription,
TaskList.find, Parser's FIND command, Ui.showMatchingTasks, and
Jeff wiring (Level-9).

commitResults.messageTitle: Add Checkstyle to enforce the SE-EDU coding standard
commitResults.messageBody:
Wire the Checkstyle Gradle plugin into build.gradle and add
config/checkstyle/checkstyle.xml and suppressions.xml, adapted from the
AddressBook Level 3 sample referenced in the SE-EDU tutorial
(https://se-education.org/guides/tutorials/checkstyle.html). The rule
set enforces the intermediate Java coding standard already required by
this project's conventions, with Javadoc checks suppressed for test

commitResults.messageTitle: Wire the JavaFX Gradle plugin into build.gradle
commitResults.messageBody:
Add the org.openjfx.javafxplugin plugin (javafx.controls module,
version 21.0.7) so JavaFX classes and native libraries resolve on the
classpath, and register a runGui task to launch the upcoming GUI
separately from the existing text-mode "run" task.

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract Ui message text into reusable format* methods
commitResults.messageBody:
Each show* method now delegates to a same-named format* method that
builds and returns the message text instead of printing it. Behavior
for the console UI is unchanged; the format* methods let the upcoming
JavaFX GUI reuse the exact same message text without duplicating it or
printing to stdout.

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract Jeff.getResponse for reuse by the console UI and a GUI
commitResults.messageBody:
Pull the command-execution switch out of main() into a new
getResponse(String) method that returns the response text instead of
printing it, using Ui's new format* methods. main() now calls it and
prints the result itself, so the console behavior is unchanged. Also
move task loading into a static initializer so it runs regardless of
which entry point (console or GUI) starts Jeff.

This is prep for the JavaFX GUI, which will call getResponse directly
instead of duplicating the command logic.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add a very basic JavaFX GUI for Jeff
commitResults.messageBody:
MainApp lays out a single window: a read-only, wrapped TextArea
transcript, a TextField for typing commands, and a Send button (Enter
in the field also sends). Every command is delegated to
Jeff.getResponse, so the GUI adds no chatbot logic of its own; typing
"bye" exits the same way the console version does.

Main is a thin, non-Application launcher for MainApp. It exists
because the JVM prints "JavaFX runtime components are missing" and
refuses to start when the main class passed to `java -cp ...` itself
extends javafx.application.Application without a module path; routing
through a plain launcher class avoids that check. Run with
`gradlew runGui`.

Verified by launching the GUI, typing "todo read book" then "list",
and confirming the task appeared as expected.

Replace add(Task) with add(Task... tasksToAdd), backed by
Collections.addAll, so callers can add several tasks in one call
instead of one add() per task. Existing single-task call sites are
unaffected since varargs accepts a lone argument. Update TaskListTest
to combine its multi-add call sites and add dedicated coverage for
adding several tasks at once and adding none.

Use Java's assert statement to make explicit several assumptions that
should always hold if the code is correct, as distinct from user-input
errors (which are already handled with exceptions elsewhere):

- TaskList.add: the varargs array and every task in it must be
  non-null, since a null task would otherwise sit silently in the list
  until it causes a confusing NullPointerException much later, in
  Storage or Ui.
- TaskList.get/remove: the index must already be range-checked by the
  caller (Parser.parseTaskIndex), documenting the contract from the
  consumer side.
- Parser.parseTaskIndex: the returned index is in range, documenting
  the same contract from the producer side, as a postcondition.
- Storage.parseLine: task is non-null after the type-letter switch,
  since every branch either assigns it or returns early; this guards
  against a future case being added that forgets to assign it.
- Deadline/Event.toString: the date field(s) are non-null, since the
  constructor's parseDate() helper always either returns a valid date
  or throws before the object finishes constructing.

Also enable assertions on the `run` and `runGui` Gradle tasks, since
the JVM otherwise ignores `assert` statements unless -ea is passed
explicitly (Gradle's `test` task already enables them by default).

The MARK, UNMARK, and DELETE cases each repeated the same try/catch
scaffolding around Parser.parseTaskIndex, differing only in which
operation ran on the resolved task and in the action word used in the
malformed-number error message. Per the CS2103 code quality guide's
"Minimize Code Duplication" guideline, this kind of copy-paste-modify
pattern is a design smell: fixing a bug in the shared error handling
(e.g. changing the error wording) would otherwise require remembering
to update it in three places.

Extract the shared resolve-and-catch logic into a new private
executeTaskCommand helper that takes an IntFunction<String> for the
case-specific behaviour, and use it from all three cases. This also
shortens Jeff.getResponse, which was one of the longest methods in the
codebase.

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract per-command handler methods in Jeff.getResponse
commitResults.messageBody:
getResponse mixed two levels of abstraction: dispatching on the parsed
command, and the detailed try/catch logic for each command. This made
the switch statement span roughly 75 lines, well past the "ideally
under 30 lines" guidance in the CS2103 code quality guide's "Avoid
Long Methods" section, and violated the Single Level of Abstraction
Principle (SLAP) it also describes, since a reader following the
switch had to context-switch into low-level error handling for each
case before returning to the dispatch logic.

Extract each case's body into its own private, single-purpose handler
method (handleMark, handleUnmark, handleDelete, handleTodo,
handleDeadline, handleEvent, handleFind). getResponse itself is now a
short dispatcher where every case reads at the same level of
abstraction: parse the command, then delegate.

commitResults.messageTitle: Replace magic numbers in MainApp's layout with named constants
commitResults.messageBody:
The window size and every spacing/padding value in the GUI layout were
unexplained numeric literals (8, 480, 600) repeated across several
calls. The CS2103 code quality guide's "Avoid Magic Numbers" guideline
flags exactly this: a reader has no way to tell whether the repeated
"8" values are the same value on purpose or a coincidence, and
changing the spacing means hunting down every occurrence.

Introduce WINDOW_WIDTH, WINDOW_HEIGHT, and SPACING constants and use
them everywhere the corresponding literal previously appeared, so the
GUI's dimensions are defined once and their intent is named.

commitResults.messageTitle: Remove comment that merely restates getStatusIcon's code
commitResults.messageBody:
The trailing "// mark done task with X" comment on the ternary in
getStatusIcon() added nothing beyond what the code already says, and
duplicated the method's own Javadoc one line above it. The CS2103 code
quality guide's "Do Not Repeat the Obvious" guideline calls this out
directly: a comment that just restates the code adds noise for readers
without adding information, and risks going stale if the code changes
but the comment isn't updated to match.

commitResults.messageTitle: Convert TaskList.find's manual loop to a stream pipeline
commitResults.messageBody:
find() built its result by hand: create an ArrayList, loop over every
task, and imperatively decide whether to add each one. That's exactly
the "filter and collect" pattern the Streams API exists for, and the
loop version needs a reader to trace the accumulator variable to see
what's being computed instead of naming the operation directly.

Replace it with tasks.stream().filter(...).collect(Collectors.toList()),
which states the intent (keep tasks whose description contains the
keyword) in one expression. Behaviour is unchanged: same filter
predicate, and Stream's encounter order preserves the original list's
order, so matches still come back in list order as documented.

commitResults.messageTitle: Convert Storage.load's manual loop to a stream pipeline
commitResults.messageBody:
load() read each line, parsed it, and imperatively decided whether to
keep the result, accumulating into a list declared before the try
block (so it could still be returned after an IOException). That shape
obscures the actual logic, which is a straightforward "parse each
line, drop the ones that failed" transformation.

Replace the loop with
Files.readAllLines(filePath).stream().map(this::parseLine).filter(Objects::nonNull).collect(Collectors.toList()),
mirroring parseLine's own Javadoc ("returns null if the line is
corrupted or unrecognized"): mapping to null and filtering it out is
the direct stream equivalent of the old "if (task != null) add it"
check. The two early returns now each return List.of() directly
instead of routing through a shared mutable accumulator that no longer
needs to exist.

commitResults.messageTitle: Convert Storage.save's StringBuilder loop to a stream pipeline
commitResults.messageBody:
save() built up its output by looping over the tasks and manually
appending each one's save-format line plus a separator to a
StringBuilder. This is a map-then-join operation, which the Streams
API expresses directly without needing a mutable accumulator the
reader has to track across loop iterations.

Replace it with
tasks.stream().map(task -> task.toSaveFormat() + System.lineSeparator()).collect(Collectors.joining()),
which produces byte-for-byte the same output as before (each task's
line immediately followed by its own separator, so an empty task list
still writes an empty string).

commitResults.messageTitle: Convert Ui.formatNumberedTasks's indexed loop to an IntStream
commitResults.messageBody:
formatNumberedTasks used a classic C-style indexed for loop just to
get both the index (for numbering) and the element (to display) at
each position, appending to a StringBuilder as it went.

IntStream.range(0, tasks.size()).mapToObj(...) expresses "for each
position, produce a numbered line" directly, without a loop counter
the reader has to relate back to tasks.get(i) themselves. Collecting
with Collectors.joining() then concatenates the lines, matching the
original StringBuilder output exactly (each line still starts with
"\n", so an empty task list still yields the header with nothing
appended).

commitResults.messageTitle: Convert Parser.Command.fromWord's search loop to a stream
commitResults.messageBody:
fromWord looped over every enum constant, returning as soon as it
found one whose word matched, and fell through to UNKNOWN otherwise.
That's a linear search, which the Streams API expresses as
filter + findFirst + orElse without a manual early-return loop.

Replace it with
Arrays.stream(values()).filter(command -> command.word.equals(word)).findFirst().orElse(UNKNOWN).
Behaviour is identical: values() is already returned in declaration
order, so the stream searches in the same order the loop did, and
orElse(UNKNOWN) reproduces the same fallback as falling out of the
loop.
Add assertions documenting internal invariants
Apply code quality guidelines from CS2103 guide

commitResults.messageTitle: Fix switch-statement indentation to match checkstyle config
commitResults.messageBody:
config/checkstyle/checkstyle.xml's Indentation module is configured
with caseIndent="4", meaning case labels are expected to be indented
one level deeper than their switch statement, with each case's body
indented one level deeper still. Jeff.getResponse and
Storage.parseLine instead used the flush style (case aligned with
switch), which fails checkstyle under this project's own configured
rule set: `./gradlew check` currently reports over 30 Indentation
errors across the two files.

Re-indent both switch statements to the style the project's own
config expects. No behavioural change; verified with `./gradlew
check`, which now passes.

commitResults.messageTitle: Fix a SeparatorWrap checkstyle violation in ParserTest
commitResults.messageBody:
checkstyle.xml requires an opening parenthesis to stay at the end of
the previous line when a statement wraps (SeparatorWrap, option
"eol"). One assertThrows call in ParserTest instead wrapped right
before the lambda's "()", putting the opening parenthesis at the
start of the new line, which checkstyle flags.

The whole call comfortably fits on one line under the project's
120-character limit, so just join it instead of wrapping it
differently. Verified with `./gradlew check`.
Set up GitHub Actions CI

commitResults.messageTitle: Add a "sort" command to order tasks chronologically by date
commitResults.messageBody:
Users had no way to view their tasks by due date once list order
diverged from add order (e.g. after deleting or adding out of
sequence). Add a "sort" command that reorders the task list so
Deadlines and Events come first, sorted chronologically by date, with
undated tasks (Todos) kept after them in their original relative
order, since there is nothing to sort them by.

- Task gains getChronologicalDate(), returning Optional.empty() by
  default; Deadline overrides it to return its due date, and Event
  overrides it to return its start date (the natural anchor for an
  event that spans a range).
- TaskList.sortByDate() sorts the underlying list in place using
  Comparator.nullsLast so undated tasks sort after dated ones, relying
  on List.sort's stability to keep undated tasks (and tasks with equal
  dates) in their original relative order.
- Parser gains the SORT command word; Jeff.handleSort() runs the sort,
  persists the new order via Storage, and reports it back through a
  new Ui.formatSortedTasks message.

Verified with new unit tests (mixed task types, no dated tasks, tied
dates) and a manual end-to-end run of the "sort" command, including
confirming the new order survives a restart (i.e. is persisted).
